27: Betrothal does not take effect - for a woman who is forbidden by negative mitzva [alone] to the one who betroths her. But the Rabbis argue, and say that it is only with those [forbidden unions] punishable by karet where the betrothal does not take effect; but with those forbidden by negative mitzva [alone], [the betrothal] does take effect. Therefore according to Rabbi Akiva, [unions] forbidden by serious negative mitzvot are equated to [unions] punishable by karet with respect to the additional prohibitions devolving thereof, [such as the ruling that] the offspring [of such unions] is a mamzer. Regarding becoming prohibited to her husband, too -- just when one has sexual intercourse with a married woman, which is punishable by karet, the woman becomes forbidden to her husband, so too when one has sexual intercourse with a widow waiting for her yavam, which is forbidden [by the negative mitzva] "the wife of the deceased shall not become that of another party, outside the family" [Deuteronomy 25:5] -- she will become forbidden to her yavam.
Is considered to be - with respect to unions forbidden by a negative mitzva
Like a woman forbidden to him - for which [the punishment would be] karet.
